current_text: 1889: summer and autumn again in Brittany, painting The Yellow Christ and The Green Christ; at Le Pouldu the Dutch painter Meijer de Haan discreetly supported him.
new_text: 1889: a third stay in Brittany, painting The Yellow Christ and The Green Christ; from August at Le Pouldu the Dutch painter Meijer de Haan paid his board and lodging in exchange for lessons.
source_note: Tate names both Christs; artfrancais: de Haan paid board

current_text: Died suddenly on the morning of 8 May 1903 in Atuona, aged 54; his neighbour Tioka found him at 11 o'clock.
new_text: Died on 8 May 1903 in Atuona on Hiva Oa, aged 54.
source_note: Date and age confirmed; Tioka/11 o'clock not found

current_text: Te tamari no atua (1896, Neue Pinakothek, Munich): a Polynesian Nativity painted as Pahura gave birth around Christmas 1896; the baby girl died in infancy.
new_text: Te tamari no atua (1896, Neue Pinakothek, Munich): a Polynesian Nativity; Pahura bore a girl around Christmas 1896 who lived only weeks, though the canvas likely predates the birth.
source_note: Shackelford: shipped July 1896, before the birth

current_text: Vollard's deal (from 1900): 300 francs a month against at least 25 paintings a year at 200 francs, plus art materials; Gauguin sent him twenty canvases in April 1902.
new_text: Vollard's deal, made after dealer Chaudet died in 1899: 300 francs a month against at least 25 paintings a year at 200 francs each, plus artist's materials.
source_note: Christie's lot essay confirms terms; April 1902 count unverified

current_text: First Tahiti trip: sailed 1 April 1891, back in France August 1893; painted Spirit of the Dead Watching (Manao tupapau, 1892) on burlap.
new_text: First Tahiti trip: sailed from Marseille 1 April 1891, back in France in summer 1893 (sources differ: July or August); painted Spirit of the Dead Watching (Manao tupapau, 1892) on jute.
source_note: Buffalo AKG: oil on jute; return month disputed
